speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: asked the Minister for Law whether the Community Disputes Resolution Tribunals can be empowered to make recommendations or require medical assessments for the claimant and respondent involved in a dispute should there be a substantial cause to believe that the respective individual is suffering from a significant medical condition which may lead to harm to themselves or others if left untreated.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: In appropriate cases, CSS may also encourage the individual to approach one of the Family Service Centres or the Agency for Integrated Care to seek referrals for medical care or social services.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Depending on the nature of the case, the CDRT can require the attendance of a party's family member during the court proceedings and encourage the relevant party to seek treatment for the medical condition.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: In cases that proceed to trial, the CDRT may issue an order requiring a respondent to cease his or her acts of unreasonable interference.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: If this order is not complied with, the CDRT may then also issue a Special Direction to the respondent requiring compliance.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: If the respondent continues to engage in acts of unreasonable interference and breaches the Special Direction, then this is an offence.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The Committee will provide more details of the review in due course.
